# Jane Doe

Jane Doe (15 May 1850 – 22 October 1925) was a fictional scientist used to
verify that the Doc2Graph extractor exercises every relation predicate defined
in the ontology. This document is not a real biography; the sentences below are
engineered so that each supported pattern fires at least once, and several
patterns fire multiple times to exercise multi-match extraction.

## Birth, family, and early life

Jane Doe was born in Paris. She was the daughter of Edmund Doe and Sophia Doe.
She was the sister of Robert Doe and Anna Doe.
She married Thomas Doe in 1880.

## Education

She studied at the University of Paris.
She enrolled at Cambridge University.
She graduated from Trinity College.

## Career

Doe worked at the French Academy of Sciences.
She also worked at the Cavendish Laboratory.
Later she worked at the Royal Institute of Technology.

She founded the Institute for Computational Studies.
She co-founded the European Mathematics Society.

She was a member of the Royal Society and the British Academy.
She was a fellow of the National Academy of Sciences.

## Publications

Doe authored "Principles of Computation".
She authored "Foundations of Algorithms".
She published "Mathematical Treatises".

She translated "The Elements of Geometry".
She edited "Annals of Mathematics".

## Influences and collaborators

She was influenced by Carl Gauss and his teacher Bernhard Riemann.
She was inspired by Leonhard Euler who pioneered modern analysis.

She was a student of Augustin Cauchy.
She was a pupil of David Hilbert.

She collaborated with Henri Poincare on differential equations.
She partnered with Bernhard Riemann on complex analysis.
She met Albert Einstein at a Solvay conference in 1911.

## Later years and death

She lived in Cambridge for many years.
She resided in Edinburgh and ran a small observatory.
She settled in London after retirement.

She died in Edinburgh.
